chapter.513010AF0D36DCAD.chapter_subtitl: Quartz and processors → one-cell ME Chest → real manual crafting → 1k autocrafting → external machines. Controller, larger cells and CPUs, P2P, wireless, Quantum and Spatial are separate expansions to choose as needed.
Read top to bottom · hover a quest to see all its connections
Open a quest to inspect all prerequisites, including links to other chapters. Item tasks check inventory; the description explains assembly and a test run.

quest.513011020C4B1739.quest_desc: Drop one Charged Certus Quartz, one Nether Quartz and one Redstone into water. Collect the Fluix crystals after the reaction; ordinary Certus cannot replace the charged crystal.
Keep some crystals for cables and crush some in the Inscriber. Fluix Dust is needed for Formation/Annihilation Cores and other network components.
quest.513011020C4B1739.title: Fluix: Crystals for Cables and Cores
quest.513011072CC6A803.quest_desc: Print a gold ingot with the Logic Press to make a Printed Logic Circuit. Then combine that circuit, Redstone and Printed Silicon in the Inscriber to obtain a Logic Processor.
Logic Processors are needed for the 1k component, terminal and Control Assembly. Prepare them before assembling the first storage network; owning the press alone does not supply finished processors.
quest.513011072CC6A803.title: Logic Press: Processors for Storage
quest.513011076371E83C.quest_desc: AE Toolsmith uses a Cell Workbench as its workstation. Give an eligible villager access to it, then check the profession and offers.
Complete a real trade with an AE Toolsmith to earn the advancement. Trading is an optional item source, not a prerequisite for processors or initial autocrafting.
quest.513011076371E83C.title: AE Toolsmith: Trade at a Cell Workbench
quest.51301108632D508B.quest_desc: This CPU uses the largest single Crafting Storage block in the standard AE2 range. Build it for a plan that justifies the capacity or as part of a chosen CPU multiblock.

It does not replace several independent CPUs for simultaneous requests. If one machine or slow dispatch is the bottleneck, improve that part of the workflow instead of endlessly increasing the plan size.
quest.51301108632D508B.title: 256k CPU: The Largest Job Plan
quest.5130110AD7EC7A65.quest_desc: After Industrial Chassis, build a Charger. It charges Certus Quartz and also turns a vanilla compass into a Meteorite Compass and a book into the AE2 Guide. These operations do not need a complete ME network.
Supply FE from the top or bottom. For a manual start, attach a Crank to either of those sides and right-click it until charging finishes. Continue with Charged Certus and the first Fluix crystals.
quest.5130110AD7EC7A65.title: Charger: Start the Quartz Line
quest.5130110B5D09E918.quest_desc: This is the largest standard AE2 component tier in this branch. It uses 64k components and costly Matrix-stage parts; plan a batch after assessing actual demand.
Choose item storage or CPU memory. Several separate cells or CPUs can be more convenient than a single largest block for every task.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × 64k ME Storage Component.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture 256k ME Storage Component. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.5130110B5D09E918.title: 256k Component: AE2’s Largest Tier
quest.5130110CD6572A2C.quest_desc: Build a Wireless Terminal from a Receiver, Terminal and Dense Energy Cell. Charge it in a Charger and bind it through the Wireless Access Point’s top-right slot.

Test retrieving and returning an item within coverage. The terminal needs charge, an active access point, network power and a channel for the access point; the portable terminal is not separate storage.
quest.5130110CD6572A2C.title: Wireless Terminal: Carry Storage Access
quest.5130110F54E2C3D4.quest_desc: A Vibration Chamber burns normal furnace fuel to power an ME network. It is an alternative source when supplying fuel is more convenient than extending an external FE line.
Connect the chamber, add a small fuel batch and check terminal operation. Add an Energy Cell for uneven demand, and check sustained generation before expanding.
quest.5130110F54E2C3D4.title: Vibration Chamber: Fuel-Based Power
quest.5130110F99A1DF48.quest_desc: Crush Certus Quartz in the Inscriber without a processor press. The dust has two early uses: smelting Silicon and crafting Quartz Glass/Quartz Fiber.
Reserve some dust for glass and cables before smelting it. Process another batch once you know which component is limiting the line.
quest.5130110F99A1DF48.title: Certus Dust: The Silicon Route
quest.51301112D49F4FE1.quest_desc: Build the Spatial IO Port using the Stellar-stage recipe. On a separate network, prepare Spatial Pylons, a Spatial Storage Cell and enough buffered energy; all components of one setup must share that network.

Follow the AE2 Guide to define the smallest volume around one cheap block. Check dimensions, required energy and efficiency in the port, insert a cell and apply a redstone pulse while standing outside the volume.
A repeat operation with the same cell swaps the current volume with the stored one. Its XYZ dimensions become fixed after first use; a different size needs a different cell.
quest.51301112D49F4FE1.title: Spatial IO: Move One Test Block
quest.5130111631820BC6.quest_desc: Build a separate small ME network with its own storage and an Interface. Place a Storage Bus from the main network against that Interface, allowing the main network to see the subnet’s storage through one port.
Keep the two networks’ cable connections separate. Quartz Fiber can share power without merging them. Avoid a reciprocal loop that exposes the same storage back into itself.
AE2’s native advancement checks a Storage Bus placed on an Interface. This subnet lesson is available at the Precision Mechanism stage; these devices do not require Stellar Alloy.
quest.5130111631820BC6.title: Subnet: Storage Bus on an Interface
quest.5130111C6FFD51A9.quest_desc: Connect the Wireless Access Point to the powered ME network and allocate a channel. To bind a finished Wireless Terminal, insert it into the access point’s top-right slot and take it back.
The access point works within its coverage area. Test the terminal close to it before extending range with boosters or additional access points.
quest.5130111C6FFD51A9.title: Wireless Access Point: Link to the Network
quest.51301121BA7BE430.quest_desc: The AE Engineer’s workstation is an ME Controller. After building the network, give an eligible villager access to one and check the profession.
The advancement triggers after a real trade with an AE Engineer. This trading branch remains optional for technology progression.
quest.51301121BA7BE430.title: AE Engineer: Trade at a Controller
quest.51301121F7B8F501.quest_desc: Network Administrator is an extreme optional target: 2,048 channel-using devices on one network. Active device count triggers the advancement; Stellar Alloy is not a condition of the advancement itself.

Plan the Controller structure, energy supply and trunk distribution around actual production areas. Normal progression only needs a network that serves your machines; there is no need to inflate it to this scale.
quest.51301121F7B8F501.title: Challenge: 2048 Active Channels
quest.513011285F6711C0.quest_desc: Attune a pair to FE with a compatible energy item and link it with the Memory Card. Connect an FE source to the input and a compatible consumer to the output.
The transport ME network must already have power and channels for the tunnels to work. First verify transfer from a charged buffer into one machine, then expand the load.
quest.513011285F6711C0.title: FE P2P: Remote External Power
quest.5130112A016321B8.quest_desc: Check that the encoded Crafting Pattern shows the correct input and output, for example one log producing four planks. Leave unnecessary ingredient substitutions disabled for this first exercise.
The pattern cannot execute its recipe by itself. Put it in a Pattern Provider with a Molecular Assembler beside it; a CPU will then be added to manage the request.
quest.5130112A016321B8.title: Crafting Pattern: A Known Table Recipe
quest.5130112BC0CDCCBA.quest_desc: Put a vanilla book in the Charger and finish charging it. The guide contains machine, network and subnet diagrams for the installed AE2 version, making it useful while building.

The central route in this chapter goes through processors, one storage cell and the first manual ME craft to 1k autocrafting. Wireless terminals, larger CPUs, P2P and spatial transport have separate branches.
quest.5130112BC0CDCCBA.title: AE2 Guide: Keep the Reference Nearby
quest.5130112C1D24E77E.quest_desc: A Quantum Bridge extends a network across great distances and dimensions. Its ring recipe uses Stellar Alloy, making this a late branch of an expanded ME network.

Each endpoint needs 8 Quantum Rings around one Quantum Link Chamber in a flat 3 × 3 arrangement. Prepare 16 rings and 2 chambers for both endpoints. This node’s item objective introduces the block; it does not verify the whole structure.
Cable connects to the four rings touching the central chamber; corner rings do not accept it. Both endpoints need power and loaded chunks.
quest.5130112C1D24E77E.title: Quantum Ring: Prepare Two Bridges
quest.5130112C9685F877.quest_desc: Build a Terminal from a Formation Core, Annihilation Core, panel and Logic Processor. Both cores use processors and quartz materials from the earlier branches.
One Terminal is consumed by the ME Chest recipe. Make another for wall-mounted access or the future Crafting Terminal; a terminal only exposes connected storage and adds no storage capacity.
quest.5130112C9685F877.title: Terminal: Access the Storage Network
quest.5130112D00658B23.quest_desc: Prepare an RFTools Crafter Tier 1, Formation/Annihilation Cores and Precision-stage components. This Crafter is an ingredient of the Molecular Assembler; the first Assembler does not require Dimensional Matrix.

Place the Assembler directly beside the Pattern Provider and provide power. It executes the normal crafting recipe using the supplied materials. A pattern left in the terminal or a Provider with no adjacent executor will not run that workflow.
Connect 1k Crafting Storage next. One Provider, one Assembler and one small CPU are enough for the first request.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × Annihilation Core.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture Molecular Assembler. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.5130112D00658B23.title: Molecular Assembler: Execute the Pattern
quest.5130112D86FBD3AF.quest_desc: Place a Quantum Link Chamber at the center of each 3 × 3 ring. The chamber does not connect directly to cables; it joins the network when the complete endpoint is correctly assembled.
Each chamber takes one singularity from the same entangled pair. Build and power both endpoints before proceeding to pairing.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × Fluix Pearl.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture ME Quantum Link Chamber. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.5130112D86FBD3AF.title: Quantum Link: The Center of Each Endpoint
quest.513011310DD7B8C1.quest_desc: Obtain a Silicon Press. The initial four presses can be obtained from a Mysterious Cube in a meteorite; an existing press can be duplicated in the Inscriber using the JEI recipe.
Print Silicon into Printed Silicon. All three finished processors use it, so a shared batch is convenient. This node’s inventory task checks the press itself; the following lessons explain its use.
quest.513011310DD7B8C1.title: Silicon Press: Every Processor’s Base
quest.513011399BE50497.quest_desc: Install Wireless Boosters in the access point when its base range is insufficient. They increase coverage and energy consumption together.
Test the most distant work area and use enough boosters for it. For scattered buildings, several access points may be more convenient than maximizing one.
quest.513011399BE50497.title: Wireless Booster: Coverage Where Needed
quest.5130113F18CF3F87.quest_desc: Build a 16k Item Storage Cell when stock quantities exceed the convenient capacity of smaller cells. Add it alongside existing cells without replacing the entire store.
Use a Cell Workbench to configure allowed types for controlled filling. If you plan to dismantle a source cell into components, make sure its data has been moved and the cell is empty first.
quest.5130113F18CF3F87.title: Item Cell 16k: A Dedicated Resource Cell
quest.51301142E35FA369.quest_desc: Place an Annihilation Plane facing a test block and provide destination storage on its subnet. It removes a supported block or item at its working face when storage can accept the result.

For selective collection, restrict the subnet’s available storage, for example with a configured Storage Bus. Test one block and its result in a chest before using the Plane beside important structures.
quest.51301142E35FA369.title: Annihilation Plane: Collect into Chosen Storage
quest.5130114314B68D20.quest_desc: Smelt Certus Quartz Dust in a furnace to obtain Silicon. Then use the Silicon Press in the Inscriber to make Printed Silicon.
Ordinary Silicon is feedstock; Printed Silicon is the part used for final processor assembly. The last step requires the printed part.
quest.5130114314B68D20.title: Silicon: Smelt, Then Print
quest.51301145AC657CE8.quest_desc: Build an ME Chest and insert one Item Storage Cell 1k. Connect it to the powered ME network. The chest has its own cell access, so a Drive or Gold Chest is not required to begin.
Insert a few items and retrieve one. Next, connect a Crafting Terminal to the same network. This storage setup also supports the first 1k CPU; the Drive’s ten cell slots are a separate expansion.
quest.51301145AC657CE8.title: ME Chest: The Smallest Working Store
quest.51301148D4813782.quest_desc: The pack recipe uses an RFTools Crafter Tier 2 and additional technology components. Add a Co-Processing Unit to a valid CPU when the executors can accept work faster.

A Co-Processor increases Provider batch dispatch and permits more simultaneous steps within one plan. It does not speed up an external machine’s recipe or give the same CPU a second independent request.
quest.51301148D4813782.title: Co-Processor: Parallel Steps Within a Job
quest.5130114905904323.quest_desc: The 4k component uses smaller 1k components, a Calculation Processor, Quartz Glass and Dimensional Matrix. This is where scaling begins after the first working network.
Choose its purpose: an item cell expands storage, while 4k Crafting Storage expands CPU memory. Making both variants is not required to reach the next component.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × 1k ME Storage Component.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture 4k ME Storage Component. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.5130114905904323.title: 4k Component: The First Expansion Choice
quest.5130114BF00256A0.quest_desc: A Fluid Cell Housing is used for a fluid storage cell. Its materials differ from the item-cell shell, so check the recipe before crafting a batch.
A finished 1k Fluid Cell also has a direct recipe. A separate housing is useful for component stock, but is not a mandatory step for the first fluid store.
quest.5130114BF00256A0.title: Fluid Housing: A Shell for Fluids
quest.51301150484DEC3C.quest_desc: Build a Wireless Receiver from a Fluix Pearl, Quartz Fiber and metal. It is a component of the access point and portable terminal; holding it alone does not open storage.
Basic wireless access is available at the Precision Mechanism stage. First, add a Wireless Access Point to the working ME network.
quest.51301150484DEC3C.title: Wireless Receiver: Portable Access Component
quest.513011540D59EE53.quest_desc: Put Certus Quartz in a powered Charger and remove the Charged Certus after the operation finishes. Ordinary and charged crystals serve different roles in recipes.
Set aside Nether Quartz and Redstone for the next step. Charged Certus starts the water reaction that produces Fluix.
quest.513011540D59EE53.title: Charged Certus: Prepare the Reaction
quest.513011543F29EA68.quest_desc: The AE Specialist uses 16k Crafting Storage as its workstation. Place a block of that type where the villager can reach it and check that the correct profession is assigned.
Complete one real trade with the specialist. The profession does not require a 64k/256k CPU, Quantum Bridge or every other trader.
quest.513011543F29EA68.title: AE Specialist: Trade at 16k Crafting Storage
quest.513011562F81FD24.quest_desc: Place the Pattern Provider on a powered ME network with a free channel and insert the encoded Crafting Pattern. When a CPU accepts a request, the Provider sends the required ingredients to an adjacent executor.

A Molecular Assembler executes an ordinary crafting-table recipe. A machine recipe instead needs a Processing Pattern and a route that returns the finished product; the two setups serve different workflows.
quest.513011562F81FD24.title: Pattern Provider: Dispatch Ingredients
quest.513011578532ED51.quest_desc: Attune a tunnel pair to the item type with a compatible item such as a chest or hopper, then link it with the Memory Card. The pair gives external item transport access to the output inventory.

For a test, push items into the input with a hopper or active pipe and place a chest at the output. Two passive chests beside tunnels do not create a flow by themselves. P2P types are separate options; every type need not be built.
quest.513011578532ED51.title: Item P2P: Carry an Item Stream
quest.5130115B3F92B69A.quest_desc: Turn the 1k Component into an Item Storage Cell 1k using a housing or the direct finished-cell recipe. Insert it into the ME Chest in the next step.
The cell limits both item quantity and the number of distinct types. Start with a few ordinary materials; keep damaged tools and items with varying data separate from bulk feedstock.
quest.5130115B3F92B69A.title: Item Cell 1k: The First Item Storage
quest.513011613E92ADD0.quest_desc: Covered Cable adds a covering to ordinary ME cable and is the base for Smart Cable. It retains the same 8-channel limit.
Use colors to make branch wiring readable, then use Smart Cable where actual channel load needs to be visible. Color alone does not create an independent subnet if other blocks still connect it.
quest.513011613E92ADD0.title: Covered Cable: Prepare for Diagnostics
quest.51301162B4562E25.quest_desc: Attune a pair to the fluid type with a compatible bucket or bottle, then link it with the Memory Card. Connect fluid transport to the input and a tank to the output.
A pump or pipe must actually feed fluid into the input. Start with a small amount and check that the destination tank accepts it; the tunnel does not create fluid or replace a pump.
quest.51301162B4562E25.title: Fluid P2P: Flow Between Tanks
quest.51301163BFF719DB.quest_desc: Choose 16k Crafting Storage for requests with more intermediate materials. The recipe uses a Crafting Unit and 16k component, so a previous 4k CPU is not required.
Check a real request’s plan and memory requirement before starting it. This block is also the AE Specialist’s workstation in the optional trading branch.
quest.51301163BFF719DB.title: 16k CPU: Memory for Recipe Chains
quest.513011659DFC96EC.quest_desc: Print a diamond with the Engineering Press, then combine the Printed Engineering Circuit with Redstone and Printed Silicon. The result is an Engineering Processor.
The first ME Chest does not need this processor. ME Drive and the Pattern Encoding Terminal do, so this branch joins the basic storage route before the first autocrafting setup.
quest.513011659DFC96EC.title: Engineering Press: Drive and Patterns
quest.5130116CC5036025.quest_desc: First, successfully store and restore the test block. The native Spatial Explorer advancement requires the player to be stored in spatial storage; owning a port or cell alone is insufficient.

Before entering, arrange an independently tested way back or a helper at the outside port. Every entity inside the defined volume moves with its blocks, so run the experiment only after checking the return route.
quest.5130116CC5036025.title: Spatial Explorer: Plan Entry and Return
quest.5130116D325212F4.quest_desc: Include a Crafting Monitor in a solid rectangular CPU multiblock. Its face displays the current job, which is useful beside a dedicated workshop.
The Monitor adds neither memory nor processing parallelism. Detailed status is also available by opening the CPU or the terminal’s job view.
quest.5130116D325212F4.title: Crafting Monitor: Read CPU Activity
quest.5130116FD5A290E7.quest_desc: Build a 1k Fluid Storage Cell from a 1k component and the corresponding materials or housing. Insert it into an ME Chest or Drive; an item cell does not provide fluid storage.
For a test, attach an Import Bus to an external tank and configure the required fluid. Verify input, then a small output through an Export Bus. Leave room for the channel and stored fluid.
quest.5130116FD5A290E7.title: Fluid Cell 1k: The First ME Fluid Store
quest.5130117628101229.quest_desc: Connect the Energy Acceptor, future ME Chest and terminal with Fluix Glass Cable. Ordinary cable carries up to 8 channels; a controller-free network has a total allowance of 8 devices that require a channel.
If a connected device remains inactive, check power, the cable path and occupied channels. Changing an ordinary cable’s color or covering does not increase that limit.
quest.5130117628101229.title: Fluix Cable: Connect the First Network
quest.5130117C40A8D2E1.quest_desc: The pack’s Drive recipe uses a Gold Chest, Engineering Processors, cables and Precision-stage components. It expands an existing ME Chest setup when one cell slot is no longer enough.
Insert the required cells into the Drive and connect it to the network. An empty Drive stores no items. Some cells can be dedicated to bulk resources; all ten slots need not be filled at once.
The first autocrafting setup also works with an ME Chest. A Drive is later required as an ingredient of the Controller recipe.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × Engineering Processor.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture ME Drive. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.5130117C40A8D2E1.title: ME Drive: Expand to Ten Cells
quest.5130117C8CDC4800.quest_desc: Build a Dense Energy Cell from ordinary Energy Cells and Precision-stage components. It increases stored network energy, not item capacity or channel count.
Add it when a small buffer repeatedly empties during brief peaks. It is also an ingredient of the portable Wireless Terminal, keeping basic wireless access possible before Dimensional Matrix.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 2 × AE2 Energy Cell.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture Dense Energy Cell. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.5130117C8CDC4800.title: Dense Energy Cell: A Larger AE Reserve
quest.51301182CE3A5863.quest_desc: Make a finished 4k Item Storage Cell using a 4k component and housing or the direct recipe. Insert it into a powered ME Chest or Drive and check the added capacity.
This tier increases stored quantity but does not remove the distinct-type limit. Adding another cell may be more useful when many different items are involved.
quest.51301182CE3A5863.title: Item Cell 4k: More Everyday Stock
quest.5130118AC1E7A654.quest_desc: Make a Blank Pattern after testing the first ME network. A blank pattern contains no recipe and does not yet tell the network how to manufacture an item.
Next, insert it into a Pattern Encoding Terminal. Use a simple log-to-planks recipe with readily available feedstock for the first exercise.
quest.5130118AC1E7A654.title: Blank Pattern: A Recipe Carrier
quest.5130119BD717861F.quest_desc: After Dimensional Matrix, craft the Controller using the pack recipe. It consumes a Drive and components from several technology branches, making it a deliberate expansion of an already working store.

Each Controller face can supply up to 32 channels through dense cable. Split these into ordinary 8-channel branches. Separate Controllers on one network do not add their limits together; expansion uses a valid connected Controller structure.
After rebuilding, check devices, power and channel paths. The first 1k CPU does not require this step; take it when the network actually needs more channels.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × Engineering Processor.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture ME Controller. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.5130119BD717861F.title: ME Controller: Beyond Eight Channels
quest.5130119E287D7DB8.quest_desc: An Item Cell Housing combines with a storage component to make a finished item cell. Spare housings are convenient when expanding storage in batches.
JEI also provides direct finished-cell recipes using glass, metals and a component. A separately crafted housing is therefore not mandatory for the first cell.
quest.5130119E287D7DB8.title: Item Cell Housing: A Reusable Shell
quest.513011A5B6C4DF0D.quest_desc: Make Quartz Fiber from quartz dust and glass. It is used in Fluix Glass Cable, which connects the first storage device and terminal.
Placed on its own, Fiber shares only power between networks. It does not merge their items or channels, which is useful for the subnets in the external-processing branch.
quest.513011A5B6C4DF0D.title: Quartz Fiber: The Cable Base
quest.513011AA8F084F8E.quest_desc: Prepare a supply of Certus Quartz. Some crystals will become charged quartz and Fluix; others will become dust, silicon and Calculation Processors. Keep a reserve instead of converting the entire supply into one intermediate.
Choose an available crystal source in JEI. Budding quartz from a meteorite is a longer-term farming option; the first processor only needs a small batch.
quest.513011AA8F084F8E.title: Certus Quartz: Processor Feedstock
quest.513011AAD4652E6F.quest_desc: Craft a Crafting Terminal from a Terminal, Calculation Processor and crafting table. Connect it to the powered ME Chest with a cell and an available channel. Stored items should appear in the terminal.

Keep, for example, one cobblestone in ME storage and craft planks from a log through the terminal grid. Completion requires a real craft in a connected, active terminal while network storage still contains at least one item. Crafting at an ordinary table or merely obtaining a terminal does not satisfy the condition.

You can now add simple input from an external chest: attach an Import Bus to it and connect the bus to ME. It pulls items into the network; a Storage Bus instead exposes the external inventory’s contents. Neither task requires autocrafting.
This proves manual crafting and access to live storage. An automatic request additionally needs a pattern, Pattern Provider, Molecular Assembler and CPU, introduced next.
quest.513011AAD4652E6F.quest_subtitle: Craft an item in a powered ME terminal
quest.513011AAD4652E6F.title: First Craft in a Live ME Terminal
quest.513011AF7E8D7059.quest_desc: The native Network Apprentice advancement is awarded when one ME network has 8 channel-using devices. This is a diagnostic exercise after basic autocrafting, not a prerequisite for the first run.
Check active devices and Smart Cable indicators. A controller-free network can reach these 8 channels; a ninth channel-using device needs a different arrangement or a Controller.
quest.513011AF7E8D7059.title: Challenge: 8 Active Channels
quest.513011B5F7F592D8.quest_desc: Prepare an Ender IO Crafter and the processors required by the pack recipe. Crafting Unit is available at the Precision Mechanism stage and is the base for CPU blocks.
A plain Crafting Unit has no job memory. Combine it with an additional 1k Storage Component to make 1k Crafting Storage; keep the existing item storage cell available for the network.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × Calculation Processor.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture Crafting Unit. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.513011B5F7F592D8.title: Crafting Unit: The CPU Base
quest.513011BB9E9B9B54.quest_desc: Use a 64k component for a large item cell. Decide which production stock it should accept before installation so an uncontrolled farm does not crowd out useful materials.
Control continuous surplus at its source or route it to separate external storage exposed by a Storage Bus. A larger cell only delays overflow.
quest.513011BB9E9B9B54.title: Item Cell 64k: Large Production Stock
quest.513011BBBBE02633.quest_desc: Crush Fluix in the Inscriber. Its dust is used in Formation Cores, Annihilation Cores, energy components and Fluix Pearls; it cannot replace whole crystals in every recipe.
The first terminal needs both cores. Keep some finished dust alongside Logic Processors so new ports do not require restarting the quartz line.
quest.513011BBBBE02633.title: Fluix Dust: Cores and Energy Buffering
quest.513011BBCA06FEA6.quest_desc: The 16k component uses 4k components and Matrix-stage materials. The recipe needs internal components, not already filled storage cells.
Choose this tier when storage demand or a larger planned request justifies the cost. A finished Item Cell 4k or 4k CPU is not a mandatory intermediate milestone.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × 4k ME Storage Component.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture 16k ME Storage Component. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.513011BBCA06FEA6.title: 16k Component: The Next Memory Tier
quest.513011C1618FC593.quest_desc: A complete quantum bridge has two endpoints, each with eight Quantum Rings around one Quantum Link Chamber. The complete kit is 16 Rings, two Chambers and two Quantum Entangled Singularities from the same pair.
Insert one singularity into each chamber, power both endpoints and keep their chunks loaded. The tasks verify counts; matching pair data and a functioning connection must be checked after assembly.
The tasks check each material and quantity without consuming it. Hold the kit before placing it, then complete the separate formation or operation check where this quest has one.
quest.513011C1618FC593.title: Quantum Bridge: Both Endpoints
quest.513011C40B19897D.quest_desc: After Dimensional Matrix, upgrade to a Wireless Crafting Terminal using the pack recipe. It adds a manual crafting grid to portable storage access.
Charge and bind the new terminal, then perform a simple craft within coverage. Automatic requests still depend on the base network’s CPUs, patterns and executors.
quest.513011C40B19897D.title: Wireless Crafting: A Grid Away from the Workshop
quest.513011C6833500D4.quest_desc: Craft Control Assembly and Energy Acceptor using the pack recipes. Supply external FE to the Acceptor and connect ME cables and devices to it.
The Acceptor supplies network power, but stores no items. Start without a Controller: one storage cell, a terminal and a few service devices fit in a small network.
quest.513011C6833500D4.title: Energy Acceptor: Power the ME Network
quest.513011CBF904C144.quest_desc: Build a 256k Item Storage Cell for a genuinely large volume of chosen resources. This is an optional storage branch, not a requirement for wireless access, a Quantum Bridge or spatial storage.
Check stored quantity and types after starting production. Even the largest standard cell has finite capacity and type slots, so retain production controls and separate overflow routes.
quest.513011CBF904C144.title: Item Cell 256k: Capacity for a Chosen Job
quest.513011CF924A9057.quest_desc: Use 64k Crafting Storage for large plans with many intermediate operations. More memory accommodates a larger plan, while an external furnace or Infuser still processes at its own speed.
If materials remain marked as expected, inspect the Processing Pattern’s output-return route. More memory cannot fix an incorrectly connected machine output.
quest.513011CF924A9057.title: 64k CPU: Large Multi-Step Batches
quest.513011CFBA3A9CF5.quest_desc: Build an Inscriber and supply FE or AE. It works as a standalone machine before Precision Mechanism: presses make printed circuits, and the final operation combines a circuit, Redstone and Printed Silicon.
Start by operating it manually: check the recipe, the required upper/lower slots and free output space. Later automation can use side-specific slots or the non-sided mode.
Circuit presses are not consumed by printing. The Inscriber also has separate Certus and Fluix crushing recipes that do not use a processor press.
quest.513011CFBA3A9CF5.title: Inscriber: Manufacture Processors
quest.513011D36DC0B032.quest_desc: Use the Calculation Press with Certus Quartz in the Inscriber to make a Printed Calculation Circuit. Keep the press for later batches.
The next step combines this circuit with Redstone and Printed Silicon. Precision Mechanism uses a Calculation Processor, so this line is completed at the Industrial Chassis stage.
quest.513011D36DC0B032.title: Calculation Press: Print on Certus
quest.513011D4AD7B73EE.quest_desc: Network Engineer counts 128 channel-using devices on one network. This is an optional engineering exercise for a large base, not a requirement for the Controller, P2P or the next CPU.
Distribute the load across Controller faces and dense trunks. Check that every device is active and that they do not share an overloaded 8-channel bottleneck.
quest.513011D4AD7B73EE.title: Challenge: 128 Active Channels
quest.513011DA15992023.quest_desc: Prepare 16k components and a Quantum Processor for the pack’s 64k recipe. It can serve an item cell or a CPU handling large multi-step requests.
A separate later use is a Matter Condenser in singularity mode. It takes a storage component directly; 64k provides enough buffer capacity for one singularity.
Guaranteed return of consumed components: 1 × 16k ME Storage Component.
Claim the refund after you or your team actually manufacture 64k ME Storage Component. An item in storage or an already completed quest alone does not prove crafting.
quest.513011DA15992023.title: 64k Component: Large Batches and Singularity
quest.513011DEEBB429E9.quest_desc: Make 1k Crafting Storage and connect it to the same network. This single block is already the smallest working CPU; extra Units, Co-Processors, a Controller or a 4k component are not needed for this test.

Check the setup: an ME Chest with a cell and feedstock, power, a terminal, a Provider containing the pattern, and an adjacent Assembler. Request a small batch of planks in the terminal, confirm the calculation and wait for the result to return to storage.

This quest’s objective checks possession of the CPU block. Verify the automatic cycle yourself using the job status and returned output. If the request cannot start, check the active CPU, known recipe, feedstock and channels.
Each separate CPU handles one request. More memory permits larger or more complex batches; two independent simultaneous requests need two CPUs.
quest.513011DEEBB429E9.quest_subtitle: The first CPU for autocrafting jobs
quest.513011DEEBB429E9.title: 1k CPU: The First Automatic Order
quest.513011DF59EDD6B8.quest_desc: Attune a pair to redstone and link it with the Memory Card. Supply a lever signal at the input and place a lamp at the output for a visible test.
After testing, replace the lamp with the required machine control. The transport network still needs power and channels even when it carries only a redstone signal.
quest.513011DF59EDD6B8.title: Redstone P2P: Carry a Control Signal
quest.513011E0DFFECB6C.quest_desc: Make two ME P2P Tunnels and a Memory Card. Place the input and output on a separate powered transport ME network; each tunnel needs one of its channels. Feed the channel source into the input’s exposed face and connect consumers to the output.

Shift-right-click the input with the Memory Card to save its frequency, then right-click the output normally to link it. Check the shared frequency and both active endpoints, then connect one test device.
A pair carries up to 32 channels in standard mode. Keep the transport network separate from the channels it carries, and do not nest ME P2P inside ME P2P.
quest.513011E0DFFECB6C.title: ME P2P: One Pair, One Clear Route
quest.513011E167D89EF9.quest_desc: Combine a Crafting Unit with a 4k component for 4k Crafting Storage. Use it when a job plan no longer fits in 1k or when another independent CPU is needed.
A single Storage block is already a CPU. If several CPU components are combined, they must form a solid rectangular prism without gaps; the combined CPU still handles one request at a time.
quest.513011E167D89EF9.title: 4k CPU: Modestly Larger Requests
quest.513011E6243A5B01.quest_desc: Combine a Printed Calculation Circuit, Redstone and Printed Silicon in the Inscriber. Take the finished Calculation Processor: this completes the first processor line.
Return to Main Route and craft Precision Mechanism next. It unlocks Control Assembly, Energy Acceptor and a small ME network; Dimensional Matrix is not needed yet.
quest.513011E6243A5B01.title: Calculation Processor: Unlock Precision
quest.513011E89C668AA7.quest_desc: Build a Pattern Encoding Terminal from a Crafting Terminal and Engineering Processor. Connect it to the same ME network and insert a Blank Pattern.
Select Crafting Pattern mode, enter a log-to-planks recipe and encode the pattern. Processing Pattern mode is for external machines and is introduced after the first completed test order.
quest.513011E89C668AA7.title: Pattern Terminal: Encode a Recipe
quest.513011EFF7B42EB6.quest_desc: Replace a short cable segment near storage with Smart Cable. On a Controller network it shows that segment’s channels; on a small controller-free network it shows total network-wide channel use. This helps explain why another device is inactive.
This is still an ordinary 8-channel branch. If real expansion is needed, plan a Controller and dense trunk in the next branch; another Smart Cable does not add capacity.
quest.513011EFF7B42EB6.title: Smart Cable: See Occupied Channels
quest.513011F21184218C.quest_desc: Place a Formation Plane on a separate powered subnet with its working face aimed at an empty space. Select block-placement mode, feed one cheap block through an Interface and verify the result.
The subnet controls exactly what reaches the Plane. Start with one block type and limited input; add the required filters and controls for a farm once a single cycle works.
quest.513011F21184218C.title: Formation Plane: Controlled Placement
quest.513011F37B07AD68.quest_desc: Connect an Energy Cell to the ME network and let it charge. It stores AE energy and buffers short demand spikes from network devices.
The buffer does not replace generation: if average consumption exceeds supply, it will empty. Check its charge during a real autocrafting request.
quest.513011F37B07AD68.title: Energy Cell: Buffer Demand Peaks
quest.513011F60668F4F2.quest_desc: After testing normal autocrafting, encode a Processing Pattern for one sand into one glass. Place a separate Pattern Provider above a vanilla furnace, insert the pattern and load furnace fuel manually.

An Import Bus below the furnace must pull the finished glass into the same ME network. Request one operation: the Provider dispatches sand for the CPU, the furnace processes it, and the Import Bus returns the declared output. The CPU keeps waiting if the glass does not return.

An Export Bus continuously supplies configured items, while a Provider dispatches a specific requested batch. An Interface can provide a return buffer; a Storage Bus exposes an external inventory. Keep the explicit Import Bus return for this first exercise.

Before extending this to a more complex machine, test its sides, power and consumables manually. A Metallurgic Infuser, for example, needs its infusion-material input configured separately; the pattern’s item list does not configure the machine.
quest.513011F60668F4F2.title: Processing Pattern: Machine and Return
quest.513011F797E11624.quest_desc: Craft a 1k Storage Component from Certus, Redstone and a Logic Processor. This is an internal component, not a finished item storage cell.
Use the first component for an Item Storage Cell 1k. Later, make another for 1k Crafting Storage: item storage and crafting-job memory have different roles.
quest.513011F797E11624.title: 1k Component: Memory for Two Jobs
quest.513011FD8979C4DD.quest_desc: Charge a vanilla compass in the Charger. The Meteorite Compass helps locate sky stone and meteorites, where you can find materials for growing Certus and the initial presses.
This is an exploration branch. If another source already supplies the required resources, continue the quartz line without making a compass expedition mandatory.
quest.513011FD8979C4DD.title: Compass: Find a Meteorite
quest.513011FEDA3CDB61.quest_desc: Run Dense Smart Cable from the Controller to a distribution point. In standard AE2 channel mode it carries up to 32 channels, and its indicator shows the trunk’s load.
Connect small cable parts and terminals through ordinary cable branches. Each such segment again has an 8-channel limit; check the complete path from Controller to device.
quest.513011FEDA3CDB61.title: Dense Smart Cable: A 32-Channel Trunk
